title: The Corrádi–Hajnal theorem on vertex-disjoint cycles
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Corrádi–Hajnal theorem (1963): every finite simple graph on at least 3k vertices with minimum degree at least 2k contains k vertex-disjoint cycles. Cycles are closed walks that are cycles in Mathlib's sense; the theorem is also stated with the definition of disjoint cycles of the registered Erdős–Pósa entry (k pairwise disjoint vertex sets, each inducing a subgraph that is not acyclic). Both hypotheses are shown to be needed: for k ≥ 2 the complete graph on 3k − 1 vertices has minimum degree 3k − 2 ≥ 2k and no k disjoint cycles, and for m ≥ 2k the complete bipartite graph K_{2k−1, m} has at least 3k vertices and minimum degree 2k − 1 and no k disjoint cycles. Mathlib has cycles and minimum degree but not this theorem.
